A.K.Alikutty vs Food Inspector on 21 December, 2017

1

 This Criminal Revision Petition Having Come Up For Admission On
21-12-2017, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following:
 B. Kemal Pasha, J.
 `````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````
 Crl.R.P. No.1553 of 2017
 `````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````
 Dated this the 21st day of December, 2017
 O R D E R

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
2.

What is under challenge is the judgment in ST No.1151/2008 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Tirur and the judgment in Criminal Appeal No.163/2013 of the Additional Sessions Court-II, Manjeri.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Tirur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Relying on the decision reported in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010 (4) KLT 706 (SC)], this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455] had held that the provisions under Section 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are mandatory and the same are applicable to all the food items.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010 (4) KLT 706 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The question involved in this case is the non-compliance of the mandatory provisions contained under Section 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
As there was a divergent view in the matter, the decision in Gopalakrishnan (supra), along with the other decisions of the learned Single Judges, was referred to the Division Bench.

The Division Bench of this Court in Crl.R.P. No.1814/2002 considered the said question and has disposed of the matter through order dated 17.11.2015, thereby upholding the view taken by this Court in Gopalakrishnan (supra).
5. Matters being so, the case against the petitioner in ST No.1151/2008 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Tirur, is illegal.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Tirur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The matters involved in the said case are quite unnecessary in view of the decisions noted supra and, therefore, the judgments of the courts below as against the petitioner are liable to be quashed.

In the result, this Crl.R.P. is allowed and the judgment in ST No.1151/2008 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court-I, Tirur, and the judgment in Criminal Appeal No.163/2013 of the Additional Sessions Court-II, Manjeri, as against the petitioner, are set aside, and the petitioner is acquitted.
